references.text: Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab and sent messengers to summon Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel. This is the original account that Joshua refers to.
The entire chapter describes how Balak tried to get Balaam to curse Israel, which is the event Joshua reminds the people about.
Balaam's blessings of Israel instead of curses, showing how God protected His people from Balak's plans.
Continuation of Balaam's prophecies and blessings over Israel, despite Balak's desire for a curse.
Moses reminds the people that Balak hired Balaam to curse them, but the Lord would not listen to Balaam and turned the curse into a blessing.
Balaam son of Beor was killed along with the kings of Midian, showing the consequence of his actions against Israel.
The Israelites also killed the prophet Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
Jephthah refers to Balak and asks if he ever fought against Israel, confirming the historical event.
The prophet Micah reminds the people what Balak king of Moab planned and how Balaam son of Beor answered him.
Revelation refers to Balaam's teaching, which taught Balak to set a trap for the Israelites.
